claims.text: High-entropy alloys with optimized microstructures can undergo a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
The proposed transition can occur without temper embrittlement.
High-pressure and high-temperature processing can optimize the microstructure of a high-entropy alloy.
The relevant test conditions include the narrow temperature window in which conventional alloys undergo temper embrittlement.
Microstructure and composition optimization enhances the strength of the high-entropy alloy.
Microstructure and composition optimization enhances the ductility of the high-entropy alloy.
Precipitate formation may contribute to the proposed enhancement of strength and ductility.
The optimized high-entropy alloy will exhibit a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
The optimized high-entropy alloy will not exhibit a dramatic loss of ductility in the narrow temper-embrittlement temperature window.
Temper embrittlement in conventional alloys occurs within a narrow temperature window.
The exact processing conditions and composition needed to obtain the proposed optimal microstructure and properties are not fully understood.

contradictions.description: The outcome places a ductile–brittle–ductile transition in the specified narrow temperature window while also asserting no dramatic ductility loss there. A ductile-to-brittle transition ordinarily entails a substantial deterioration of ductility or toughness, so the proposed observable behavior is not clearly distinguished from the loss it denies.
